title: Can I Build Too?
can_do: 请求加入同伴的搭建，回应他需要桥的想法，并商量连接位置后一起把路接通。
trigger: Peer is building a road that still needs a bridge; Child asks to join and offers to build the blue bridge at the road's end.
setting: Two friends join wide toy road and bridge pieces on a home play mat.
essential_props: one road-and-bridge set: four tan road pieces and one blue bridge piece

turns.speaker: peer
turns.line: I'm building a road. It needs a bridge.

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: Can I play with you? I can build the bridge.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.line: Will your bridge join my road?

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: Yes. The blue bridge fits at the end, so the road goes on.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.line: Okay, let's build. I'll add this road piece.

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: The bridge and road fit together.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.line: We made a longer road together.

replay_cards.title: Join the animal home
replay_cards.setting: Pretend animal play on the floor
replay_cards.change: Peer has built one house and wants it to stay intact; Child offers to add another home beside it
replay_cards.challenge: Ask to join and hear that the first house must stay. Child offers a second home, but Peer thinks Child means building on top of his house. Child repairs with "No, I mean beside your house." Peer chooses a clear side for the new home; Child agrees, builds there, and both move their animals between the two homes.

replay_cards.title: Join the chalk road
replay_cards.setting: Drawing together on a clear outdoor paving patch
replay_cards.change: Peer is finishing a chalk road and wants its current line left intact; Child wants to add a parking place
replay_cards.challenge: Ask to join, propose a parking place, and let Peer choose a space that keeps his road clear. Child checks "Is it beside your road?" and requests "Can I have the chalk, please?" Peer finishes the short line and passes the chalk. Child draws the agreed parking place and both trace a route into it with their fingers.

parent_support: Keep Peer's road plan real: he asks whether the offered bridge will connect before accepting.
Let Child choose a useful contribution and show the proposed place. A small nod is enough; agreement does not require cheering or giving up either child's idea.
